items.prompt: Which radical expression is equivalent to x^(3/4)?

wrong.why: Swapped the roles of numerator and denominator, using 3 as the root index and 4 as the power.
Treated the numerator 3 as a coefficient inside the radical instead of as a power of x.
Treated the numerator as a multiplier outside the radical instead of an exponent.

items.explanation: In x^(m/n), the denominator n is the root index and the numerator m is the power, so x^(3/4) = ⁴√(x³).

items.prompt: What is the value of 25^(3/2)?

wrong.why: Multiplied 25 by 3/2 instead of treating 3/2 as an exponent.
Took the square root of 25 and then multiplied by 3 instead of cubing.
Multiplied 25 by 3 and ignored the square root.

items.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to ³√(y⁵)?

wrong.why: Put the root index in the numerator and the power in the denominator.
Subtracted the index from the power (5 − 3).
Multiplied the index and the power (3 × 5).

items.explanation: The index 3 becomes the denominator and the power 5 the numerator, so ³√(y⁵) = y^(5/3).

items.prompt: Evaluate 16^(3/4).

wrong.why: Computed 16 × 3/4 instead of using it as an exponent.
Took ⁴√16 = 2 and multiplied by 3.
Added the numerators and the denominators separately.
Multiplied the exponents instead of adding them.
Added the exponents correctly but then inverted the fraction.

items.explanation: When multiplying powers with the same base, add the exponents: 1/2 + 1/3 = 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6.

items.prompt: Which is √72 written in simplest radical form?

wrong.why: Pulled out 36 without taking its square root.
Correctly pulled out 6 but made an error with the leftover factor, writing 3 instead of 2.
Pulled out a 2 and a 6 from the wrong places and kept 6 under the radical.
Added the exponents instead of multiplying them.
Divided the exponents (2/3 ÷ 3/4) instead of multiplying them.
Added the numerators and denominators separately.

items.explanation: A power of a power multiplies exponents: (2/3)(3/4) = 6/12 = 1/2.

items.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to (27x⁶)^(2/3), x > 0?

wrong.why: Multiplied 27 by 2/3 instead of applying the exponent 2/3 to it.
Took the cube root of 27 but forgot to square it.
Added 2/3 to the exponent 6 instead of multiplying.

items.prompt: Simplify 5√2 · 3√8 to a single integer.
items.explanation: Multiply coefficients and radicands: 15√16 = 15 · 4 = 60.

wrong.why: Multiplied correctly but did not simplify √16.
Added 5 + 3 instead of multiplying.

items.prompt: Which sum is an irrational number?

wrong.why: √36 = 6 is rational, so the sum is rational; the student assumed any square root is irrational.
Both addends are rational, so the sum is rational; the student confused a long decimal with an irrational number.
√25 = 5 is rational, so the difference is rational; the student assumed any root is irrational.

items.explanation: √5 is irrational, and the sum of a rational and an irrational number is irrational. The other sums combine rational numbers.

items.prompt: Which product is a rational number?

wrong.why: A nonzero rational times an irrational is irrational, but the student thought it could be rational.
Same issue: 4 is rational and nonzero, √3 irrational, so the product is irrational.
Nonzero rational times irrational is irrational, not rational.

items.explanation: √2 · √8 = √16 = 4, which is rational. Each other product is a nonzero rational times an irrational, which is always irrational.

items.prompt: Which argument correctly shows that 1/2 + √3 is irrational?
items.answer: If it equaled a rational r, then √3 = r − 1/2 would be rational, which is false.

wrong.text: √3 has a never-ending decimal, so adding anything to it makes the sum never-ending.
wrong.why: Confused non-terminating with irrational: 1/3 also never ends but is rational.

wrong.text: Adding two numbers can only give a rational number when both are integers.
wrong.why: Wrongly believes rational sums require integers; 1/2 + 1/2 = 1 and 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4.

wrong.text: The number 1/2 is smaller than √3, so the sum cannot be written as a fraction.
wrong.why: Size comparison has no bearing on rationality.

items.explanation: Suppose 1/2 + √3 = r is rational. Then √3 = r − 1/2 is a difference of rationals, so rational, contradicting that √3 is irrational.

items.prompt: Write 4 + √(−49) in the form a + bi.

wrong.why: Chose the negative square root; the principal root of −49 is +7i.
Added 4 and 7 as if they were like terms.
Pulled out i but forgot to take the square root of 49.

items.prompt: What is the value of i²⁷?

wrong.why: Used a remainder of 1 when dividing 27 by 4 instead of 3.
Used i² = −1 without reducing the exponent properly.
Treated i² as +1 and so every even-ish power as 1.

items.explanation: Powers of i repeat every 4. 27 = 4·6 + 3, so i²⁷ = i³ = i² · i = −i.

items.prompt: Evaluate (5 + 2i)(5 − 2i). Give a real number.

wrong.why: Treated i² as +1, giving 25 − 4.
Dropped the i² term entirely.

items.prompt: A ball's height in feet after t seconds is h = −16t² + 48t + 5. What does the constant 5 represent?
items.answer: The height of the ball at t = 0, when it is released

wrong.text: The height of the ball when it is highest
wrong.why: Confused the constant term with the maximum height.

wrong.text: The time in seconds when the ball lands
wrong.why: Confused the constant with a zero of the function.

wrong.text: The speed of the ball when it is released
wrong.why: Confused the constant with the linear coefficient 48.

items.explanation: At t = 0 the terms with t vanish and h = 5, so 5 is the starting height.

items.prompt: The time T in hours to drive a trip at an average speed r mph is T = 120/r. What does 120 represent?
items.answer: The distance of the trip in miles

wrong.why: Mixed up the constant with the variable r.

wrong.text: The total travel time in hours
wrong.why: Mixed up the constant with the output T.

wrong.text: The decrease in time for each extra mph
wrong.why: Misread the constant as a rate of change.

items.explanation: Since time = distance ÷ speed, the numerator 120 is the distance traveled.

items.prompt: In the expression 5√(x + 4) − 2, what is the radicand?

wrong.why: Confused the coefficient with the radicand.
Confused the constant term with the radicand.
Included the coefficient and the root symbol; the radicand is only what is under the radical.

items.explanation: The radicand is the expression inside the radical sign: x + 4.

items.prompt: In y = −2(x − 3)² + 10, what does the coefficient −2 tell you about the parabola?
items.answer: It opens downward and is stretched vertically by a factor of 2

wrong.text: It opens upward and moves the vertex to x = −2
wrong.why: Confused the coefficient with the vertex x-coordinate.

wrong.text: It crosses the y-axis at the point (0, −2)
wrong.why: Confused the coefficient with the y-intercept.

wrong.text: It opens downward and has a maximum value of −2
wrong.why: Confused the coefficient with the maximum value, which is 10.

items.explanation: The sign of a in a(x − h)² + k sets the direction (negative means down) and |a| = 2 is the vertical stretch.

items.prompt: A club sells wristbands at price p dollars. Profit is P = (p − 4)(100 − 5p). In this expression, what does 100 − 5p represent?
items.answer: The number of wristbands sold at price p

wrong.text: The profit earned on each wristband sold
wrong.why: Confused the number sold with the per-item profit p − 4.

wrong.text: The total revenue from all wristbands
wrong.why: Revenue would be p(100 − 5p); this factor alone is not revenue.

wrong.text: The cost the club pays per wristband
wrong.why: The per-item cost is the 4 subtracted in p − 4.

items.explanation: Profit = (profit per item)(number sold). p − 4 is profit per item, so 100 − 5p is the number sold.

items.prompt: A drone is 30 m above the ground and x m horizontally from you. Its straight-line distance from you is D = √(x² + 900). Which statement is true?
items.answer: D is never less than 30, because x² cannot be negative

wrong.text: D can be as small as 0 when x = 0
wrong.why: Forgot the 900 under the radical: D = √900 = 30 when x = 0.

wrong.text: D is always equal to x + 30 meters
wrong.why: Wrongly split the square root over a sum.

wrong.text: D gets smaller as x gets larger, since x is squared
wrong.why: Reversed the effect of increasing x² inside the radical.

items.explanation: x² ≥ 0, so x² + 900 ≥ 900 and D ≥ 30, with D = 30 exactly when x = 0.

items.prompt: Which is equivalent to x² + 8x + 3 after completing the square?

wrong.why: Added 16 to complete the square but did not subtract it back.
Used 8 instead of half of 8 inside the square, then compensated with 64.
Subtracted 16 and then subtracted 3 instead of adding it.

items.prompt: The expression x² − 6x + 14 can be written as (x − 3)² + k. What is the minimum value of the expression?
items.explanation: x² − 6x + 9 − 9 + 14 = (x − 3)² + 5, and the square is at least 0, so the minimum is 5.

wrong.why: Gave the x-value where the minimum occurs.
Gave the original constant term.

items.prompt: What is the minimum value of 2x² − 12x + 7?

wrong.why: Subtracted only 9 instead of 2 · 9 = 18 after factoring out the 2.
Added 18 instead of subtracting it.
Gave the x-value of the vertex instead of the minimum value.

items.prompt: Rewrite h = −2x² + 12x − 5 by completing the square. What is the maximum value of h?

wrong.why: Subtracted 18 instead of adding it back.
Gave the x-value of the vertex.

items.prompt: Which is equivalent to 3x² + 12x + 5?

wrong.why: Added 4 inside the parentheses but did not subtract it (times 3).
Subtracted 4 instead of 3 · 4 = 12 to balance.
Did not halve the coefficient 4 inside the parentheses.
Added 5 and 7 instead of 5 and −7.
Subtracted the constants (−2 − 6) instead of adding them.
Added the exponents when combining the x² terms.

items.explanation: Combine like terms: 4x², 5x − 7x = −2x, −2 + 6 = 4.

items.prompt: Subtract: (5x² − 3x + 4) − (2x² + x − 9).

wrong.why: Did not distribute the negative sign to the second polynomial.
Distributed the negative to the first two terms only.
Added x instead of subtracting it, getting −3x + x = −2x.

items.explanation: Distribute the minus: 5x² − 3x + 4 − 2x² − x + 9 = 3x² − 4x + 13.

items.prompt: Multiply: (2x − 3)(x² + 4x − 5).

wrong.why: Made a sign error on the last product (−3 · −5).
Distributed +3 instead of −3.
Flipped the sign of −10x when combining like terms (−12x + 10x = −2x).

items.prompt: Find the coefficient of x in the simplified form of (3x − 2)(x + 4) − (x − 1)².
items.explanation: (3x² + 10x − 8) − (x² − 2x + 1) = 2x² + 12x − 9, so the coefficient of x is 12.

wrong.why: Forgot to distribute the minus onto −2x.
Ignored the second product entirely.

items.prompt: A rectangle's length is 3 cm more than its width w, and its area is 40 cm². Which equation models this?

wrong.why: Used perimeter-like addition instead of multiplying length and width.
Squared the width and added 3 instead of multiplying (w)(w + 3).
Added the length and width instead of multiplying them.

items.explanation: Area = width × length = w(w + 3), set equal to 40.

items.prompt: A ball is thrown upward from 4 ft with h = −16t² + 36t + 4. Which equation gives the times when the ball is 20 ft high?

wrong.why: Used height 0 (landing) instead of 20.
Dropped the initial height 4.
Changed the sign of the t² term.

items.explanation: Set the height function equal to the target height: −16t² + 36t + 4 = 20.

items.prompt: The square of a positive number is 36 more than 5 times the number. Write and solve an equation. What is the number?
items.explanation: n² = 5n + 36, so n² − 5n − 36 = 0, (n − 9)(n + 4) = 0, and the positive solution is n = 9.

wrong.why: The negative root, which is not positive.
Factored as (n + 9)(n − 4) and took the wrong root.

items.prompt: Painting a fence takes 4 painters 6 hours. Time t varies inversely with the number of painters n. Which equation models t?

wrong.why: Treated the relationship as direct variation.
Inverted the fraction.
Used a linear relationship with the same sum 4 + 6.

items.explanation: Inverse variation: t = k/n with k = 4 · 6 = 24.

items.prompt: A farmer uses 60 m of fence for three sides of a rectangular pen against a barn wall. The sides perpendicular to the barn have length x. Which inequality says the area is at least 400 m²?

wrong.why: Subtracted only one width instead of two.
Treated it as fencing all four sides (perimeter 60).
Reversed the inequality direction.

items.explanation: The two sides use 2x, leaving 60 − 2x for the third side. Area x(60 − 2x) ≥ 400.

items.prompt: A rocket's height in meters is h = −5t² + 40t, whose graph is a parabola opening down. At what time t, in seconds, is the rocket highest?
items.explanation: The vertex is at t = −b/(2a) = −40/(−10) = 4 seconds.

wrong.why: Gave the time the rocket lands.
Gave the maximum height.

wrong.why: Satisfies the line but not the parabola.
Satisfies the parabola but not the line.
Satisfies the parabola but not the line.

items.explanation: At x = 3: x² − 4 = 5 and x + 2 = 5. Both equations are satisfied.

wrong.why: Gave the length instead of the width.
Divided 24 by 2.

items.prompt: A roller coaster track follows y = x² + 1 and a support beam follows y = 2x + 9. They meet at two points; what is the positive x-coordinate of the meeting point?
items.explanation: x² + 1 = 2x + 9, so x² − 2x − 8 = 0, (x − 4)(x + 2) = 0, and the positive solution is x = 4.

wrong.why: The other (negative) solution.
Used the constant of the line.

items.prompt: Solve the system y = √(x + 5) and y = x − 1. Which gives the solution(s)?

wrong.why: Is an extraneous solution from squaring; it gives y = −2 on the line but √4 = 2.
Did not check for extraneous solutions.
Set the radicand equal to zero.

items.explanation: Squaring: x + 5 = x² − 2x + 1, so x² − 3x − 4 = 0, giving x = 4 or −1. At x = −1: √4 = 2 but −1 − 1 = −2, so it is extraneous. Only x = 4 works.
